q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a home inverter or UPS?
title: Inverter and UPS carbon footprint per unit
short: Add the bought-in parts per unit: transformer copper and steel, circuit board, metal or plastic cabinet and cables, each with a supplier figure. Add assembly, burn-in testing electricity and packing, then divide by units built. Count the battery separately.

ul: Transformer with copper winding and lamination steel.
Assembled circuit board and heat sinks.
Winding and varnishing if made in-house.
Burn-in and load testing, which can draw real power.

p: Report per inverter by VA rating, and state whether the battery is included. A battery usually weighs several times more than the inverter.

example.title: Worked example: home inverter and UPS unit per unit (one month)
lines: Plant total: 17,750 / 5,000 = 3.550 kg CO2 per unit
Add transformer, board and cabinet for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
